mainEntity.name: How many calories does my dog need each day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply resting energy (70 × weight in kg to the power 0.75) by a factor for life stage and activity. A typical neutered adult uses about 1.6 times resting energy. A 55 lb dog needs roughly 1,250 kcal.

mainEntity.name: How many cups of food is that?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide the calories by the kcal per cup on your food label. Foods range from about 300 to 450 kcal per cup, so the same dog can need very different cup amounts.
A common guideline is that treats should be no more than 10% of daily calories. Reduce the meal portion by the same number of calories.
It is a 1 to 9 scale where 4 to 5 is ideal. You should feel the ribs under a thin fat layer and see a waist from above. A score of 7 or more means the dog is overweight.

mainEntity.name: How often should I feed my dog?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most adult dogs do well on two meals a day, and puppies on three or four. Weigh the food rather than scooping, since a cup can vary by 20%.
